name: Wilted Flower
tldr: 🥀 marks an ironic disaster, a dead plan, or an exaggerated reaction to making things worse.

contextMeanings.meaning: 🥀 jokingly says that a plan, situation, or conversation has collapsed beyond repair.
contextMeanings.example: the group chat is dead after i accidentally sent that voice note 🥀

contextMeanings.meaning: 🥀 can simply refer to a drooping or dying flower, though the sad image often adds drama to the message.
contextMeanings.example: the bouquet looked better before it started wilting 🥀

contextMeanings.meaning: 🥀 can dramatize a romantic apology, but it tends to spotlight the sender's hurt instead of acknowledging the other person's pain.
contextMeanings.example: i know i hurt you, and i feel terrible about it 🥀

contextMeanings.meaning: 🥀 reads as overwrought or meme-like in a professional thread, especially when serious consequences are being discussed.
contextMeanings.example: i missed the deadline because the export broke again 🥀

platformNotes.note: On TikTok, 🥀 fits the meme-heavy language used to announce that a plan, trend, or reveal has completely collapsed. It is most likely to work when the surrounding video clearly establishes the joke.
In an Instagram caption or comment, 🥀 can exaggerate a bad result, such as a ruined outfit or disastrous trip. In a post about genuine grief, its meme quality can make the reaction feel careless.

In iMessage, 🥀 can add dramatic self-deprecation after a mistake or failed plan. Used after an apology, though, it can draw attention to the sender's wounded feelings rather than the harm they caused.

In Slack, 🥀 may look casual beside a minor workplace mishap, but it feels awkward beside serious feedback, blame, or a difficult team update. A written apology or a straightforward problem summary is safer.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z commonly understands 🥀 through irony: the situation is dead, ruined, or hilariously beyond saving. Outside that ironic use, many younger senders avoid it because it feels too meme-like for sincere moments.

Millennials generally recognize the joke but approach 🥀 more cautiously because of its younger meme quality. For a serious offense or loss, they are more likely to expect words rather than the emoji alone.
Some older recipients may take the mournful artwork more literally than younger emoji users do. The dramatic or Gothic impression can also make 🥀 feel excessively heavy in a sincere conversation.

warnings.title: It looks like a meme in a grief thread
warnings.description: After someone discloses a death, 🥀 can be taken as trivializing the loss or trying too hard. Send a candle, a rose, or a direct expression of sympathy instead.

warnings.title: It turns an apology toward the sender
warnings.description: 🥀 can make the sender appear focused on their own wounded feelings, so it rarely closes the emotional loop. Use 🙏, 🫂, or a clear sentence that names the harm and apologizes for it.

seoDescription: What does 🥀 mean? It usually marks an ironic disaster, a botched plan, or an over-the-top wounded reaction, but can read as a meme in grief.

longForm.overview:
🥀 is a drooping flower, and the image carries two sharply different possibilities. In ordinary conversation, its main job is ironic acknowledgment: “this is ruined,” “the plan is dead,” or “that whole situation has collapsed.” That makes it a natural punctuation mark after a botched plan, a spectacular group-chat disaster, or a reveal that the speaker has made the situation worse. Because it looks wounded rather than cheerful, it also lets people present their own failure with exaggerated melodrama.

The harder problem is that its artwork is unmistakably mournful. A friend receiving 🥀 after disclosing a death may not know whether the sender is sharing grief or making the loss into a meme. Likewise, in an apology, 🥀 can shift attention from the person who was hurt to the sender’s own wounded feelings. In both cases, a plain sentence is safer than making the emoji carry the emotional work.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
People reach for 🥀 when something has spectacularly gone wrong. It can follow a canceled plan, an embarrassing reveal, a failed group project, or a message that made the sender look ridiculous. The joke is essentially “this is dead,” but the drooping flower makes the failure look extra dramatic.

The emoji also appears when someone wants to advertise their own disappointment in a deliberately exaggerated way. In a romantic thread, it may dramatize guilt or wounded pride. That use can quickly become self-centered, though. The most successful messages put the irony first and make the surrounding text clear enough that nobody has to guess whether the sender is joking.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Do not use 🥀 when someone has shared a death, serious illness, or another genuine loss. Although the artwork could resemble a memorial flower, younger senders often use the emoji ironically, so the message can land as a meme or as an awkward attempt at solemnity. A candle, a rose, or a sentence expressing sympathy is more dependable.

It is also a poor apology emoji. 🥀 tends to perform the sender’s wounded feelings and leave the recipient to focus on the sender’s pain. Millennials may be especially cautious with its younger meme quality, while Gen Z may parse it quickly but still expect plain words after a serious offense. Use 🙏, 🫂, or an actual apology.
longForm.howToReply:
When 🥀 is plainly joking about a disaster, you can match it with another 🥀, a laughing face, or a short comment about what went wrong. If the situation is less obvious, ask whether they are being serious before treating the flower as a joke.

If someone sends 🥀 as an apology, do not mirror the wounded-flower drama. Name the harm, say you are sorry, and explain what you will do differently. If it arrives after a loss disclosure, respond with warmth and specificity instead of the emoji. When it lands on your own mishap, you can own the joke in one sentence; that keeps the melodrama from swallowing the actual point.

faqs.question: What does 🥀 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: In most contexts, it means the situation or his plan is completely dead. In a romantic message, it can also dramatize guilt, but it may make him seem more focused on his own hurt than on yours.

faqs.question: Is 🥀 flirty?
faqs.answer: Not usually. The wilted flower is more commonly ironic or dramatic than romantic, and using it after an apology can make the message feel overdrawn rather than affectionate.

faqs.question: What does 🥀 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, 🥀 usually marks a spectacular failure, a ruined plan, or something hilariously beyond saving. It works best when the caption or video makes that ironic meaning clear.

faqs.question: Should I send 🥀 to someone who is grieving?
faqs.answer: Probably not. Despite its mournful appearance, many people use 🥀 as a meme, so it can seem flippant in a grief thread. Send a candle, a rose, or a direct message of sympathy instead.

conversationExamples.message: our saturday plan is officially dead after nobody checked the weather 🥀
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is joking that the trip or outing collapsed because of poor planning. Laugh, commiserate, or suggest another plan.

conversationExamples.message: i'm sorry i ignored you all night, it really hurt when you saw it 🥀
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is trying to apologize but sounds focused on their own hurt. Respond to the actual behavior rather than the dramatic emoji.

conversationExamples.message: the presentation is completely dead after the projector stopped working 🥀
conversationExamples.interpretation: This can work among teammates who already know the event was chaotic. In a client thread, explain the problem plainly and omit the emoji.
The sender may be trying to mark the family's grief, but the emoji can make the tribute feel like a joke. A candle or a direct remembrance is safer.

conversationExamples.message: i said one nice thing and accidentally made it sound like an insult, so anyway social media is dead 🥀
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is exaggerating their embarrassment for comic effect. A laughing reply or a quick reassurance works; do not treat the wilted flower as a serious emotional confession.
